newsitem.title: USA: Jury continues deliberating in USAir suit.
newsitem.headline: Jury continues deliberating in USAir suit.

text.p: A federal jury continued deliberating Thursday on whether US Airways Group was at fault in the 1994 crash of a DC-9 near Charlotte/Douglas International Airport that killed 37 people.
Deliberations had begun at about 5:15 p.m. EST (2215 GMT) on Wednesday, stopped about an hour later Wednesday evening, and began again at 9:00 a.m. (1400 GMT) Thursday.
The jurors had had no questions about the case by early evening Thursday. Court officials had not said when deliberations might adjourn for the day.

Separately, an alternate juror in the Flight 1016 case had said after being dismissed Wednesday that he probably would have found USAir to blame for the crash, but would probably not have awarded punitive damages.
If the jury decides that USAir was not only at fault but deserves to be punished for the crash, it could become the first U.S. jury to award punitive damages in a commercial aviation case.
